sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**
Nestle India Limited (NESTLEIND) reported a consolidated total income of ₹202,604.2 million for the financial year ended 31st March 2025, with a profit after tax of ₹33,145.0 million. The company's revenue from operations net of GST was ₹200,775.0 million, and its profit from operations was ₹43,104.1 million. NESTLEIND also reported an investment in an associate company, Dr. Reddy's and Nestlé Health Science Limited, with a carrying amount of ₹5,750.3 million as of 31st March 2025. The associate company's revenue was ₹2,148.8 million, with a profit of ₹1,607.9 million for the financial year ended 31st March 2025.

**Investment Thesis**
Our investment thesis for NESTLEIND is based on its stable financial performance, with a focus on its revenue from operations and profit from operations. The company's diversified product portfolio and strong brand presence in the Indian market are key strengths. Additionally, the investment in the associate company, Dr. Reddy's and Nestlé Health Science Limited, provides an opportunity for growth in the health science segment. With an earnings per share of ₹34.38 and a dividend per share of ₹25.50 (interim: ₹17.00 and final: ₹8.50), NESTLEIND offers a relatively stable return on investment. However, the lack of comparable information for the associate company due to the recent investment made on 24th July 2024, may pose some uncertainty. Overall, we believe that NESTLEIND's strong financials and growth opportunities make it an attractive investment opportunity in the Indian consumer goods sector.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body:
Nestle India (NESTLEIND) operates within a single operating segment, namely Food, which encompasses various product groups including Milk Products and Nutrition, Prepared Dishes and Cooking Aids, Powdered and Liquid Beverages, and Confectionery. The company's business activity is primarily focused on the Indian market, with no assets held outside of India. For the financial year ended 31st March 2025, the company reported revenue from operations of ₹200,775.0 million, with ₹192,926.7 million attributed to the Indian market and ₹7,848.3 million from outside India.

In terms of segment breakdown, the company does not have multiple operating segments, and therefore, the entire revenue is attributed to the Food segment. The revenue from external customers is primarily driven by the Indian market, which accounted for approximately 96% of the total revenue for the financial year ended 31st March 2025. There is no single customer that accounts for more than 10% of the company's revenue, indicating a diversified customer base. The company's operating cycle is ascertained as 12 months, which is based on the nature of products and the time between acquisition of assets for processing and their realization in cash and cash equivalents.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body:
The financial performance of NESTLEIND for the year ended 31st March 2025, reveals a total income of ₹202,604.2 million, comprising revenue from operations net of GST of ₹200,775.0 million, other operating revenues of ₹1,240.6 million, and other income of ₹588.6 million. The profit before exceptional items and tax stood at ₹41,566.5 million, with an exceptional item expense of ₹2,908.2 million, resulting in a profit before tax of ₹44,474.7 million. The net profit (PAT) for the year was ₹33,145.0 million. 

In comparison to the fifteen-month financial year ended 31st March 2024, the total income decreased by ₹42,814.3 million. The profit after tax also decreased from ₹39,328.4 million to ₹33,145.0 million. The earnings per share (EPS) for the year ended 31st March 2025, was ₹34.38. The company's retained earnings balance as of 31st March 2025, stood at ₹40,089.5 million. The return on equity ratio was 88.9% for the year ended 31st March 2025, indicating a decline from the previous year's ratio of 108.5%.

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet health of NESTLEIND, as reflected in the accounting ratios, indicates a current ratio of 0.8 times as of 31st March 2025, down 9% from 0.9 times in the previous fifteen-month period. The debt-equity ratio has increased to 0.3 times from 0.1 times, representing a 190% variance, primarily due to short-term borrowing taken for meeting working capital requirements. 

The company's cash flow position is not directly provided in the excerpts. However, the debt service coverage ratio of 33.7 times suggests that the company has sufficient earnings available to service its debt obligations. The negative net capital turnover ratio of (21.1) times indicates negative working capital, which may impact the company's cash flow management. Further information on the company's cash flow statement would be necessary to provide a more comprehensive analysis of its balance sheet health and cash flow position.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of Nestle India Limited has provided commentary on the tax expense for the year ended 31st March, 2025. According to the filing excerpts, the income tax expense comprises of current tax and deferred tax, with the current income tax charge calculated on the basis of the tax laws enacted or substantively enacted at the end of the reporting period. The provision for current tax for the period includes an estimated tax expense of ₹10,646.3 million, which has accrued on the profit for the period from 1st April 2024 to 31st March 2025. Additionally, the company has recognised a deferred tax expense of ₹171.1 million, which is based on temporary differences between the carrying amount of assets and liabilities in the balance sheet and its corresponding tax base.

The management has also mentioned that deferred tax assets are recognised only to the extent it is probable that future taxable profits will be available against which such assets can be utilised. However, the filing excerpts do not provide information on the net profit or net worth of the company, or the revenue from operations for the year ended 31st March, 2025. Therefore, we are unable to comment on these aspects of the company's performance.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The 'Key Risks' section of this report highlights potential concerns that may impact NESTLEIND's financial performance. One key risk is the investment in Associate Company, Dr. Reddy's and Nestlé Health Science Limited, which was made on 24th July 2024, with a carrying amount of ₹5,750.3 million as of 31st March 2025. The associate company's financial performance, with revenue of ₹2,148.8 million and profit of ₹1,607.9 million for the financial year ended 31st March 2025, may have a significant impact on NESTLEIND's consolidated financials.

Another risk is the consolidation adjustments of ₹1,886.0 million, which is a significant amount compared to the carrying amount of the investment. However, without further information on the nature of these adjustments, it is difficult to assess their potential impact on NESTLEIND's financials. Additionally, the company's exposure to associate company's liabilities, with total current liabilities of ₹1,127.7 million and total non-current liabilities of ₹17.3 million as of 31st March 2025, may also pose a risk to NESTLEIND's financial stability.

Recent Developments
The company's recent developments include a change in the face value of its equity shares, which were sub-divided from ₹10 to ₹1, effective from the record date of 5th January 2024. As a result, one equity share with a face value of ₹10 was sub-divided into 10 equity shares with a face value of ₹1 each. For the financial year ended 31st March 2025, the company reported a total income of ₹202,604.2 million, comprising revenue from operations of ₹200,775.0 million, other operating revenues of ₹1,240.6 million, and other income of ₹588.6 million. The company's profit after tax stood at ₹33,145.0 million, with an earnings per share of ₹34.38.

The Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of ₹10.00 per equity share for the financial year 2024-25, amounting to ₹9,641.6 million, subject to approval by the shareholders at the ensuing Annual General Meeting. The company's revenue from external customers in India was ₹192,926.7 million, while revenue from outside India was ₹7,848.3 million. The company does not have any significant business operations or assets outside India. Additionally, there is no single customer that accounts for more than 10% of the company's revenue for the financial year ended 31st March 2025.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for NESTLEIND is supported by the company's recent investment in Associate Company, Dr. Reddy's and Nestlé Health Science Limited, with a 49% ownership interest and a carrying amount of ₹5,750.3 million as of 31st March 2025. The associate company has reported a profit of ₹1,607.9 million for the financial year ended 31st March 2025, with revenue of ₹2,148.8 million. This investment could potentially contribute to NESTLEIND's future growth and profitability.

The bear case, on the other hand, is limited by the lack of comparable information for the associate company, as the investment was made on 24th July 2024. As a result, it is challenging to assess the long-term impact of this investment on NESTLEIND's financial performance. Our base case assumes that the associate company will continue to perform in line with its current financial trends, with NESTLEIND's 49% share in the associate's net assets valued at ₹3,864.3 million as of 31st March 2025. However, without additional information on the company's overall financial performance, including its consolidated revenue from operations and net profit, it is difficult to provide a more comprehensive assessment of the company's outlook.
